# Engine modules maintained by Ferraloom

Source: https://github.com/Pumpkin-MC/Pumpkin.git

Base commit: `5b53f064af8708ba33fcaa533b81ca29a53a3310`.

Only `pumpkin-core`, `pumpkin-world`, and `pumpkin-command` are vendored. Cargo patches the pinned Git dependency with these modules. Other engine crates keep their original pinned Git source and shared type identities. The nested workspace inherits upstream package, lint, and dependency settings, with unvendored Pumpkin paths redirected to that exact revision.

The world's two generated feature-definition includes are copied from the same base revision's `pumpkin-data` sources so the world crate can compile independently. Referenced upstream test fixtures, the status icon, and management schema are retained with the asset notices.

The world crate extracts its embedded world-preset JSON and an igloo template test fixture into Cargo's build output from the checksum-verified official 26.3 server, using `PUMPKIN_MINECRAFT_SERVER_JAR` or the repository's ignored reference cache. This replaces source-tree includes that depended on the upstream data crate's extraction location. Official executables and extracted datapacks are not committed.

Local patches cover status connection handling, command block states and predicates, forced chunk loading, datapack discovery, 26.3 world storage, and ore-generation arithmetic. Further patches implement execute score stores, clock restoration and saving, ordered entity saves, retryable region writes, explicit flush completion, and Java LZ4 stream terminators with bounded compression levels. Anvil region writes synchronize the file before reporting completion. Stronghold cache initialization runs its small one-time calculation sequentially to avoid Rayon workers re-entering the same `OnceLock`; chunk generation remains parallel. The nested lockfile pins the additional development dependencies needed to run engine-module tests independently, with the same local module patches as the root build.

Additional patches persist a shared server scoreboard, snapshot player watch transitions before releasing generation tickets, and cancel abandoned postprocessing requests through owned activation demands. Scheduled block/fluid ticks use their own eligibility range. Server autosaves serialize complete snapshots and flushes, including during simulation freeze. Ordinary terrain unloading honors save-off, with independent entity storage and explicit save/shutdown overrides.

Durable NBT writes propagate encoding failures and replace files through synchronized staging files, preserving previous player, chunk, entity and metadata saves on failure. Block simulation owns terrain leases and watcher references until callbacks finish and block entities are snapshotted; block-entity migration and ticking use the block range with loaded entities. Player transfers and respawns share a transition gate, and spectators can receive existing ready chunks without requesting view generation. Legacy scoreboard paths are read before starting an empty board, and new saves use the current namespaced path. Command-block result counts reset for each execution.

Terrain eviction coordinates with World-owned block entities before unpublishing, including unwatched halo inventories and retained spectator views. External inventory handles defer the final snapshot. Player backups recover before login admission; failed recovery cannot create a replacement default player. Cooking blocks retain current signed timers and fuel speed, rescale progress on ignition, and keep lava bucket crafting remainders. Score/team selectors use scoreboard identities and distinguish absent scores from zero. Forceload query and list have separate results and failure behavior. Independent auxiliary metadata saves are attempted even if level.dat fails.

Player snapshots retain their capture order, and per-UUID session ownership spans admission through final player and advancement saves. Advancement JSON uses ordered atomic writes. Renewed terrain tickets cancel stale block-entity unloads. Fill-destroy placement runs without chunk guards, uses distinct deferred neighbor callbacks, and sends final resulting states to clients. Data-modify registration retains every source provider and places insertion sources under the required index. Alive entity selectors exclude dying living entities before their removal.

Recursive data merging preserves sibling fields, validates source objects before mutation, and matches selected partial-failure and primitive-array paths. Missing-path execute conditions count matches without throwing. Identifier parsing rejects the exact parent namespace, and command redirects can resolve the final tree node. Server command storage persists namespaced gzip NBT through manual, automatic and shutdown saves, including during save-off; modern files take precedence over discovered legacy files. Diode and tripwire removal now notify the relevant neighbors and preserve tripwire's scheduled pulse behavior. Paired tests cover these selected outcomes; complete command, redstone and storage parity remains unverified.

Live data patches update retained barrel, chest, trapped-chest, sign and hanging-sign instances and keep complete persistence separate from client tags. Container contents and pending loot share one publication transaction; stale generation cannot overwrite replacements. Sign submissions remain literal, privileged clicks respect allow-op gates, and command callbacks run after releasing text locks. Opaque component faces are retained and data edits refuse them before path callbacks. Further patches cover ordinary recursive data merge and stale teleport acknowledgments. Selected native and client checks cover these paths; complete container, component and multiplayer parity remains unverified.

Upstream license and asset notices are retained. Ferraloom's differential suite records behavior changes against the official server. See the Git history for local patches.
